key_locators.statement: jj46 shell-model Hamiltonian constructed for Z<=50, N>=82
129Pd ground state 7/2-, predicted 19/2- seniority-core isomer at Ex = 1.903 MeV

Calculated Sn = 1.524 MeV in jj46 (1.461 MeV in FRDM; 1.780 MeV in AME2012), placing the 19/2- isomer at Qn = 0.379 MeV (0.442 MeV in FRDM; 0.123 MeV in AME2012) above 128Pd(0+)+n, while decay to 128Pd(2+, 1.311 MeV) is energetically closed
Two-potential Bohr-Sommerfeld calculation yields l=9 partial neutron half-life T1/2(n)=0.3–10 us competing with calculated E2 gamma decay (tau_E2=0.955 us); model prediction within Yuan et al. (2016)
Predicted 5- isomers in odd-odd 132,134In and 130Ag with long lifetimes from pi-nu E2 cancellation

bibliographic.title: Discovery of New Isotopes 160Os and 156W: Revealing Enhanced Stability of the N = 82 Shell Closure on the Neutron-Deficient Side

key_locators.statement: Discovery of 160Os (N=84) and 156W (N=82) in 106Cd(58Ni, 4n) at SHANS/HIRFL
160Os ground-state alpha: E_alpha = 7080(26) keV, T1/2 = 201(+58/-37) us, sigma = 5.4(+1.2/-1.0) nb

files.reading_coverage: Verified core text, printed p. 897 unit audit (184 us microseconds), Fig. 3 level scheme (intermediate K=3 bandhead ~988 keV, 841/943 keV M1 transitions to g.s.b. 4+/2+), and g_K=0.87(14) discussion; raw RITU/GREAT focal plane event-by-event calorimetry data unverified

bibliographic.title: Nuclear isomers in superheavy elements as stepping stones towards the island of stability

key_locators.statement: Firm identification of 266(2) ms 8- isomer at Ex = 1293 keV and higher-lying 184(3) us (microseconds, confirmed by visual audit override of pdftotext mu->m misencoding) isomer at >= 1.2 MeV above the 8- state in 254No

266 ms isomer decays via 53-keV E1 into intermediate 2-QP K=3+ band (bandhead at ~988 keV, with 841- and 943-keV M1 transitions de-exciting to the ground-state band 4+ and 2+ states, respectively; previous assertion of 943-keV bandhead retracted)

Assuming rotational model validity, branching ratios in the intermediate K=3+ band give g_K = 0.87(14), identifying two-proton {1/2-[521]p x 7/2-[514]p}3+ bandhead and constraining the 1/2-[521] Nilsson orbital correlating with spherical 2f5/2 above Z=114
The 184 us isomer feeds the 8- isomer via 606-keV gamma and conversion cascade; spin change 6–8 units (J>=14), with (16+) 4-QP assignment characterized as highly tentative on experimental grounds

Author discussion of 266 ms 8- isomer configuration: decay to two-proton 3+ band suggests two-proton assignment, but two-neutron configuration and state-mixing are also discussed; configuration assignment is non-unique in literature
